_why: ONE fixture, parsed by BOTH halves of the history_record Rust->TS seam.
src-tauri/src/history.rs asserts serde PRODUCES and CONSUMES exactly these objects for
them and yields the same two booleans. Change the key casing on one side and BOTH suites go
red together -- which is the entire point. AGENTS.md records the alternative (bead
sparkle-16y6h): two agents built the two halves of a wire against a frozen field list, both
suites passed, the merge was clean, and the shipped feature never once ran.
THE THREE STATES ARE THE WHOLE REACHABLE SPACE. history_record used to be INSERT OR IGNORE
returning nothing, so a second message under an already-taken id was discarded with no error,
no log and no return value -- 199 of 200 on-screen concierge messages in the founder's live DB
had the same id as an existing row but DIFFERENT text. `collided` is the alarm for exactly
that. `{inserted: true, collided: true}` is UNREPRESENTABLE and is deliberately NOT here.
NO NULLS, BY CONSTRUCTION. Both fields are plain Rust bools, never Option, so serde always
emits both keys with a true/false value and the TS side is `boolean`, not `boolean | null`.
If either ever becomes an Option, it crosses the wire as an EXPLICIT null (never as an absent
key), the TS type must become `boolean | null` -- NOT `boolean | undefined`, which excludes
null -- and a null case must be added to this file. See shared/history-range-wire.json's

The id exists and its stored text is byte-identical. Benign idempotent re-capture (a re-render, a rehydrate, a double subscribe) -- the case INSERT OR IGNORE was designed for. NOT an alarm.
